identity.name: Brandenburg-Prussia
alt_names: Electorate of Brandenburg and Duchy of Prussia

land.text: the Hohenzollern Electorate of Brandenburg, the core of the realm and its seat at Berlin

predecessors.note: The Electorate of Brandenburg dossier ends August 1618; this page gives only the year 1618.

land.text: the Duchy of Prussia, inherited by the Brandenburg Electors on Albert Frederick's death in 1618 and held as a fief of the Polish Crown until 1656/57

predecessors.note: Cleves, Mark and Ravensberg (Rhineland-Westphalia) were already Brandenburg's after the Treaty of Xanten (1614) and have no row of their own.

land.text: the whole realm: after the Crown Treaty of 16 November 1700 Frederick crowned himself 'King in Prussia' at Königsberg on 18 January 1701; Brandenburg 'was de facto treated as an integral part of the kingdom'

successors.note: A change of title, not of land. The Brandenburger Gold Coast passed to the kingdom too (renamed Prussian Gold Coast Settlements on 15 January 1701).

capitals.name: Berlin
capitals.note: Berlin was the main Brandenburg seat and Königsberg the Prussian capital (Brandenburg-Prussia page); George William 'withdrew in 1637 to the relatively untouched region of Prussia' and died at Königsberg on 1 December 1640 (George William page), leaving Schwarzenberg to run the government.

rulers.name: John Sigismund
rulers.note: Added by reviewer eu-09-k: the Margraviate of Brandenburg page has the elector John Sigismund inherit the Duchy of Prussia in 1618 ('his son-in-law John Sigismund inherited the Duchy of Prussia'); George William succeeded in 1619 (George William page).

rulers.name: George William
rulers.note: 'In 1619, George William inherited the Margravate of Brandenburg and the Duchy of Prussia'; died 1 December 1640 at Königsberg. The 1618-1619 Elector-Duke is John Sigismund (Margraviate of Brandenburg page; entry added by reviewer eu-09-k).

rulers.name: Frederick (Elector; crowned King in Prussia as Frederick I on 18 January 1701)
rulers.note: The Brandenburg-Prussia page gives the Elector-Duke period 1688-1701; the Kingdom of Prussia page gives the coronation.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page dates the realm 'Brandenburg-Prussia (1618 – 1701)' and has the Electors inherit the Duchy of Prussia in 1618, but Cliopatria's first shape begins 1619. The 1619 shape (Brandenburg, Cleves-Mark-Ravensberg, Ducal Prussia) applies one year earlier.

correction.text: the 1619 shape applied to 1618: the union of Brandenburg and the Duchy of Prussia on Albert Frederick's death

keyframe_review.note: 87.5 k km2: Brandenburg, Cleves-Mark-Ravensberg and Ducal Prussia. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible; Cliopatria's own rows Electorate of Brandenburg (44.3 k) and Duchy of Prussia (38.5 k) plus the Rhenish lands sum to about this. Ducal Prussia stayed a fief of the Polish Crown until 1656/57 (page); the shape draws it as Brandenburg-Prussia's own.
Same land as 1619 (87.4 k km2). The page names no territorial change in 1626-1628; it says only that Brandenburg changed sides several times in the Thirty Years' War.
Same land as 1619 (87.5 k km2); no territorial change on the page for 1629-1631.

76.5 k km2: Cliopatria drops about half of Brandenburg proper (48 of 87 cells). The page says Gustavus Adolphus sacked Küstrin and Frankfurt an der Oder and then bombarded George William in Berlin (1630-1631) and that George William stayed Elector (he joined the Heilbronn League after Lützen, 1632), so the land was fought over, not lost. Kept whole; the Oder zone is a contest (ledger 1631-1648).

correction.text: Brandenburg, Cleves-Mark-Ravensberg and Ducal Prussia whole: the 1636 shape, with the Swedish-fought Oder zone drawn as a contest by the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 88.5 k km2, Brandenburg whole again. The page dates no change in 1636; the Peace of Prague (1635) is the nearest dated event (the George William page says the Heilbronn League was dissolved following the 1635 Peace of Prague).

74.6 k km2: Brandenburg proper is again about half drawn (39 of 86 cells). George William died on 1 December 1640 still Elector at Königsberg, having 'withdrew in 1637 to the relatively untouched region of Prussia'; the page names no loss of land. Kept whole, with the Swedish-fought Oder zone contested.

correction.text: the 1636 shape: Brandenburg, Cleves-Mark-Ravensberg and Ducal Prussia whole

keyframe_review.note: 58.8 k km2: Cliopatria leaves 3 of Brandenburg's 86 cells to the Elector (Ducal Prussia and Cleves only). The Great Elector page says only that Berlin 'had suffered greatly from the Swedish occupation during the Thirty Years' War' and had 6,000 people left in 1648; it dates neither the occupation nor any cession, and he inherited Brandenburg in 1640. Kept whole, occupation read as the Oder contest. Unverified: page budget; a gap-filler should open the page on his 1641 armistice with Sweden.

correction.text: the 1636 shape: Brandenburg, Cleves-Mark-Ravensberg and Ducal Prussia whole

keyframe_review.note: 58.7 k km2, same loss of Brandenburg as 1642 and the same reading (Swedish occupation, not cession; the page gives no date). Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: the 1636 shape: Brandenburg, Cleves-Mark-Ravensberg and Ducal Prussia whole

keyframe_review.note: 106.4 k km2: +Farther Pomerania, Halberstadt, Minden. 'Brandenburg-Prussia received Farther Pomerania, and the Bishoprics of Magdeburg, Halberstadt, Kammin, and Minden' (Westphalia, signed 24 October 1648), but 'the treaty did not decide the Swedish-Brandenburgian border in the Duchy of Pomerania', which was settled in 1653 (Treaty of Stettin, Brandenburg-Prussia page). The Pomeranian zone is therefore a contest 1648-1653 in the ledger and a gain in 1653; Magdeburg was only a succession right until 1680.
108.8 k km2: +Lauenburg-Bütow and Draheim. The page dates the Treaty of Bromberg to 1657, so the shape holds from 1657, not 1659.

correction.text: shape unchanged; holds from 1657, when the Treaty of Bromberg gained Lauenburg-Bütow and Draheim

keyframe_review.note: 108.9 k km2, one cell more than 1659; no change on the page between 1660 (Peace of Oliva confirmed Hohenzollern sovereignty in Prussia) and 1674.

108.8 k km2. Brandenburg held much of Swedish Pomerania (except Rügen) from 1677 to 1679 (Stettin besieged 1677, Great Elector page; restored December 1679, Saint-Germain page); Cliopatria does not draw that land as Brandenburg's, and the ledger carries it as a contest.

124.1 k km2: +the former Swedish east bank of the Oder (29 June 1679, 'except for Gollnow and Damm'), +Magdeburg (incorporated 1680, Brandenburg-Prussia page), +the Gold Coast cells in Ghana. The shape holds from 1679/1680, not 1683. The Ghana cells are the colony of the Brandenburger Gold Coast dossier (vassal_start 1682), so they are removed here.

correction.text: shape without the Ghana cells; holds from 1680 (Magdeburg), the Oder strip from June 1679

keyframe_review.note: 124.8 k km2; the page has Brandenburg receive the Silesian County of Schwiebus in 1686 (returned 1694). Ghana cells removed as in 1683.

correction.text: shape without the Ghana cells; includes Schwiebus from 1686

keyframe_review.note: 124.1 k km2, a few cells fewer than 1687-1690. The page returns Schwiebus in 1694, three years after this shape begins; Cliopatria's 1691 start is not the page's date. Ghana cells removed.

correction.text: shape without the Ghana cells; Schwiebus held until 1694

keyframe_review.note: 124.8 k km2. The shape runs 1700-1717 but the realm became the Kingdom of Prussia on 18 January 1701 (Kingdom of Prussia page), so it is Brandenburg-Prussia's for 1700 and January 1701 only; the Kingdom of Prussia dossier carries the land from 1701. Ghana cells removed (the colony is its own dossier).

correction.text: shape without the Ghana cells; valid for 1700 and until 18 January 1701 only

keyframe_review.note: 1.7 k km2 of Ghana only. The page says the colony was renamed Prussian Gold Coast Settlements on 15 January 1701, 'physically abandoned by Prussia' in 1717 and sold in 1721; it is a colony of the Kingdom of Prussia, not Brandenburg-Prussia, which ended in 1701. These cells belong to the Brandenburger Gold Coast dossier.

correction.text: the Prussian Gold Coast Settlements around Cape Three Points: the colony's own dossier (brandenburger-gold-coast) and the Kingdom of Prussia's tint, not Brandenburg-Prussia

ledger.note: 1618: the Hohenzollern Electors of Brandenburg inherit the Duchy of Prussia and the two lands become Brandenburg-Prussia. The page dates the realm 'Brandenburg-Prussia (1618 – 1701)'; the Electors inherited the Duchy of Prussia on Albert Frederick's death in 1618, though it stayed a fief of the Polish Crown until 1656/57; Cleves, Mark and Ravensberg had been incorporated after the Treaty of Xanten (1614). Month (reviewer eu-09-k): the Margraviate of Brandenburg page's infobox has 'Brandenburg-Prussia: 27 August 1618', the month the electorate-of-brandenburg and duchy-of-prussia dossiers end.

region.text: Brandenburg, the Duchy of Prussia and Cleves-Mark-Ravensberg

ledger.note: 1631: Sweden fights its way into Brandenburg. Gustavus Adolphus sacked Küstrin and Frankfurt an der Oder and then bombarded George William in Berlin (1630-1631, Thirty Years' War page). The page dates no Swedish occupation of Brandenburg's later years and no cession, so the zone is drawn as the Oder towns the page names; its extent by year is a gap (the Great Elector page says only that Berlin 'had suffered greatly from the Swedish occupation').

region.text: Küstrin and Frankfurt an der Oder, sacked by the Swedes in 1630-1631

ledger.note: October 1648: Westphalia awards Farther Pomerania to Brandenburg, but 'the treaty did not decide the Swedish-Brandenburgian border in the Duchy of Pomerania' and Sweden had controlled it since 1630. The zone is drawn contested until the 1653 border treaty.

region.text: Farther Pomerania, awarded to Brandenburg-Prussia in 1648 while Sweden still held Pomerania

ledger.note: 24 October 1648: Brandenburg-Prussia is compensated with the secularised bishoprics. 'Brandenburg-Prussia received Farther Pomerania, and the Bishoprics of Magdeburg, Halberstadt, Kammin, and Minden' (Peace of Westphalia); Brandenburg-Prussia page: Halberstadt and Minden secularised, Magdeburg a succession right only (incorporated 1680), Farther Pomerania incorporated 1653.

region.text: the bishoprics of Halberstadt and Minden

ledger.note: 1648: the Swedish-Brandenburg fighting in the Mark ends with the Peace of Westphalia (signed 24 October 1648). The page dates the end of the war to 1648 ('Berlin had only 6,000 people left when the wars ended in 1648', Great Elector page); the end of the Swedish presence on the Oder is not dated separately.

region.text: Küstrin and Frankfurt an der Oder

ledger.note: 1653: the Treaty of Stettin fixes the Brandenburg-Swedish border in Pomerania. the Treaty of Stettin (1653) set the border with Swedish Pomerania

1653: Farther Pomerania is incorporated. Farther Pomerania was incorporated in 1653; the Westphalia page awards it in 1648 and says the border stayed unsettled until 1653. Cliopatria draws it from 1648.
1657: the Treaty of Bromberg gives Brandenburg-Prussia Lauenburg-Bütow and Draheim (the Treaty of Wehlau-Bromberg also confirmed Brandenburg's sovereignty in Ducal Prussia, but not Ermland).

region.text: Lauenburg-Bütow and Draheim, gained at the Treaty of Bromberg

ledger.note: 1677: Brandenburg takes Swedish Pomerania. He led a 'successful siege of Stettin' in 1677 and conquered 'much of Swedish Pomerania during the Scanian War' (Great Elector page); Saint-Germain page: Brandenburg occupied Swedish Pomerania except Rügen. The page does not date the first Pomeranian campaign; 1677 is its only dated step there.

29 June 1679: at Saint-Germain Brandenburg keeps a strip of Pomerania. It 'further gained the former Swedish eastern bank of the Oder river except for Gollnow and Damm' (Gollnow pawned for 50,000 talers, redeemed by Sweden in 1693), with 300,000 talers and the reversion of East Frisia.

region.text: the former Swedish eastern bank of the Oder, except Gollnow and Damm

ledger.note: 1679: Brandenburg gives Swedish Pomerania back. It returned Bremen-Verden and most of Swedish Pomerania to Sweden; Stettin, its last stronghold there, was restored in December 1679.

region.text: Swedish Pomerania except Rügen, returned to Sweden by December 1679

ledger.note: 1680: Brandenburg-Prussia incorporates Magdeburg. Magdeburg was incorporated in 1680 (a succession right since 1648). Cliopatria draws it from 1683. Counterpart (reviewer eu-09-k): the archbishopric-of-magdeburg dossier, which dissolves in 1680 with this state as successor ('secularised by Brandenburg'); the page has 'the Duchy of Magdeburg (incorporated in 1680)'.

region.text: the Duchy of Magdeburg (the former archbishopric)

ledger.note: July 1682: Brandenburg plants its colony on the Gold Coast. the Brandenburg African Company was founded on 7 March 1682 and an expedition in July began the fortress Großfriedrichsburg; a 16 May 1681 treaty with the chiefs had allowed a fort, and Fort Dorotheenschanze was agreed on 24 February 1684. The colony has its own dossier (drawn as a tint of the metropole), so Cliopatria's Ghana cells are removed from the shapes.

region.text: Großfriedrichsburg and the Brandenburg forts on the Gold Coast

ledger.note: 1686: Brandenburg renounces its Silesian claims in favour of the Habsburgs and receives the Silesian County of Schwiebus. Month (reviewer eu-09-k): the page ties the cession to the alliance of 22 December 1686, in which Brandenburg-Prussia 'in turn received the Silesian County of Schwiebus'.
1694: Schwiebus goes back to the Habsburgs (the page: returned in 1694).

15 January 1701: the colony passes to the new kingdom. 'On 15 January 1701, the small colony was renamed Prussian Gold Coast Settlements.' The relation continues as a colony of the Kingdom of Prussia.

region.text: the Gold Coast colony, renamed Prussian Gold Coast Settlements

ledger.note: 18 January 1701: Frederick crowns himself King in Prussia and the realm becomes the Kingdom of Prussia. Crown Treaty of 16 November 1700; 'Frederick crowned himself "King in Prussia" as Frederick I on 18 January 1701'; Brandenburg 'was de facto treated as an integral part of the kingdom'. Cliopatria's Brandenburg-Prussia shape runs on to 1717 beside the Kingdom of Prussia's from 1702.

region.text: the whole realm, continued as the Kingdom of Prussia

wars.name: Thirty Years' War

zones.text: Küstrin and Frankfurt an der Oder, sacked 1630-1631
Farther Pomerania, where Sweden held the ground and Westphalia left the border open

wars.outcome: Brandenburg changed sides several times and was devastated by Swedish and Catholic forces; at Westphalia (24 October 1648) it received Farther Pomerania and the bishoprics of Halberstadt, Kammin and Minden, with succession rights to Magdeburg.
wars.note: The Thirty Years' War page says little about Brandenburg: Brandenburg was 'ambivalent about Swedish intervention' (1630-1631), stayed out of the Heilbronn League in 1633 on that page but joined it after Lützen on the George William page. The two pages disagree on 1633; the George William page is more specific.

wars.name: Second Northern War (Brandenburg's part)
wars.outcome: Frederick William fought Sweden and Poland and changed sides in 1657: the Treaty of Königsberg (January 1656) took Ducal Prussia and Ermland as Swedish fiefs, Labiau (November 1656) gave full sovereignty, Wehlau-Bromberg (1657) confirmed it but not for Ermland and gained Lauenburg-Bütow and Draheim, and the Peace of Oliva (1660) confirmed Hohenzollern sovereignty in Prussia.
wars.note: Sovereignty over Ducal Prussia (a Polish fief until 1656/57) changed status, not borders, so no gain is recorded for it. The war's own article was not opened (page budget).

wars.name: Jülich succession invasion
wars.outcome: Frederick William invaded Jülich-Berg and the affair ended with the Treaty of Kleve in October 1651; no border moved (the Great Elector page says his title to Cleves, Jülich and Ravensberg was 'definitely recognized' in 1666).
wars.note: The page does not name the opponent; 'Duchy of Jülich-Berg' is the land invaded.

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War (Brandenburg's part)
wars.outcome: Brandenburg first allied with the Dutch Republic, made peace with France in the June 1673 Treaty of Vossem, then joined the imperial side in the Reichskrieg against France; no border moved.
wars.note: The Treaties of Nijmegen ended the war itself (Saint-Germain page); neither page gives their year.

wars.name: Scanian War (Brandenburg-Swedish War)
wars.outcome: Sweden invaded Brandenburg in 1674-1675 (Fehrbellin); Frederick William took Stettin (siege 1677) and most of Swedish Pomerania, and in the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye (29 June 1679) returned most of it, keeping the east bank of the Oder except Gollnow and Damm; Stettin was restored in December 1679.
wars.note: Years 1674-1679 from the Brandenburg-Prussia page's list of wars; the Great Elector page also records the 1678 Great Sleigh Drive in Ducal Prussia.

certainty.note: Thirty Years' War: the Swedish-held and ravaged parts of Brandenburg and Pomerania moved without a treaty line; the scattered Rhenish lands are drawn from the Cliopatria outline.
Borders fixed by treaty: Westphalia (1648), Stettin (1653), Bromberg (1657), Oliva (1660), Saint-Germain (1679). The Gold Coast forts (1682-1701) are soft.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 from the nine pages in sources (page budget 9; one was a disambiguation page opened by mistake).

Span. The page dates the realm 1618-1701 and calls it 'the historiographic denomination' for the Hohenzollern realm; Cliopatria runs 1619-1720. This dossier ends on 18 January 1701 and the Kingdom of Prussia dossier carries the land from 1701, which removes the 1702-1717 overlap of the two Cliopatria rows (drawn side by side in 1710). Cliopatria's 1718-1720 shape is 1.7 k km2 of Ghana and is wrong for this state.

Gold Coast. Cliopatria's Ghana cells (1683-1720) are the Brandenburger Gold Coast colony. A separate dossier (brandenburger-gold-coast, written by another group) holds it; here it is a vassal_start/vassal_end pair and the cells are removed from the corrected shapes. The page also records Arguin (taken over 1 October 1685) and a Saint Thomas base under Danish sovereignty (November 1685); neither has a Cliopatria shape and neither is mapped.

Thirty Years' War. Cliopatria drops half or nearly all of Brandenburg proper in 1632-1635 and 1640-1647 (48, 39 and 3 of about 86 cells). None of the pages dates a cession; they describe sack, devastation and 'Swedish occupation'. The shapes are corrected to the whole realm and the Oder towns the page names are carried as a contest with Sweden 1631-1648; the real extent and years of the Swedish-held land are a gap (a gap-filler should open the Great Elector's 1641 armistice with Sweden and the Swedish side's pages). The Thirty Years' War and George William pages disagree on 1633 (outside or inside the Heilbronn League).

Ducal Prussia. Held as a Polish fief until 1656/57 (Labiau, Wehlau-Bromberg, Oliva); Cliopatria draws it as Brandenburg-Prussia's own from 1619 and so does this dossier. The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and Duchy of Prussia dossiers may record the fief as a vassal relation; the renderer should not draw it twice. The Duchy of Prussia and Electorate of Brandenburg dossiers end August 1618; this page gives only the year 1618.

Cleves, Mark, Ravensberg. In the 1619 shape from the start (Xanten 1614); the Great Elector page says only that his title was definitely recognised in 1666. No gain is recorded.

Cliopatria dating. Magdeburg (page 1680) and the Oder strip (June 1679) appear in Cliopatria's 1683 shape; Lauenburg-Bütow (1657) in the 1659 shape; Schwiebus (1686-1694) is a handful of cells that come and go in 1687, 1691 and 1700. The verdicts say so.

Counterparts without a dossier of their own (the lump holy-roman-empire-minor-states stands in): the bishoprics of Halberstadt, Minden and Kammin and the archbishopric of Magdeburg; the Duchy of Jülich-Berg; Swedish Pomerania is inside the Swedish Empire row.

Gazetteer names used that the gazetteer lacks: Halberstadt, Minden, Świebodzin (Schwiebus), Princess Town (Ghana).

Rulers. The 1618-1619 Elector-Duke is not named on any page opened and is omitted.
